thought.title: Small Shape Regression: Custom GELU Slower than PyTorch at 1024×1024
thought.description: For small shapes (S1: 1024×1024), custom AscendC kernel achieves only 0.87x speedup vs PyTorch reference. The pybind11 wrapper overhead, tiling setup (tiling tensor allocation, CPU→device transfer, kernel launch), and suboptimal core utilization (only 8 blocks for 1024 rows ÷ 128 blockM) dominate execution time for tiny workloads.
thought.reason: Elementwise activation on small tensors is memory-bound and launch-overhead dominated. PyTorch's fused GELU has zero kernel launch overhead and uses highly optimized vector paths. Custom kernel launch overhead is fixed cost regardless of tensor size.
